findings.title: Corrupt preference file is overwritten on next save after a failed load
findings.message: On a validation failure after earlier layouts were pruned, loadPreferences returns without setting m.layouts, and preferencesPath remains set. The next customization change then calls savePreferences, which overwrites the user's invalid or too-large file. The same happens for the 'too many layouts', oversize, and parse-error cases. This contradicts the stated goal of not clobbering files, and a transient corrupt file is permanently replaced.
findings.suggestion: Treat load failures other than not-exist as non-destructive: clear preferencesPath (or keep a flag) so the file is not overwritten, or back it up before the first save.

findings.title: Temp-file cleanup and permissions are implicit
findings.message: f.Close() is called twice, which is harmless. But the deferred os.Remove runs after a successful Rename; it just fails silently. Meanwhile, the Rename error is returned as-is, which is fine. The main concern is that the directory is never fsynced after the rename, so durability is not guaranteed on a crash. This is minor, but a more serious problem is that the temp file is created with CreateTemp's 0600 mode, which only works by accident and is not set explicitly.
findings.suggestion: Call f.Chmod(0600) explicitly and avoid the redundant remove after a successful rename.
